description:
SIZED s461ar (agent AR, round 18) from a MEASURED shape table.  This task
replaces the standing "it is a feature" hand-wave with numbers, so a future
session can decide from data instead of re-deriving it.  The drops stay LOUD
either way (ruled s401/s419 6.3: the file-level lvalue-sub drops keep dropping).

WHY IT LOOKED CHEAP, AND WHY IT IS NOT.  PCL's box model already makes a
scalar an alias, and a sub call already returns the BOX rather than a copy for
the simplest shape -- `sub f :lvalue { $x }` -- so `\f()` writes through to
`$x` TODAY, with no lvalue support at all.  That is one shape out of eight.
Measured (perl 5.40.3 oracle vs ./runpcl at 33a71c9, probe
scratchpad/p2.pl, `$r = \SHAPE(); $$r = NEW;` then read the target):

    sub s1 :lvalue { $x }              perl writes through   PCL writes through  OK
    sub s2 :lvalue { return $x }       perl writes through   PCL copies          MISS
    sub s3 :lvalue { $_[0] }           perl writes through   PCL copies          MISS
    sub s4 :lvalue { ${\shift} }       perl writes through   PCL copies          MISS
    sub s5 :lvalue { substr($s,0,2) }  perl writes through   PCL copies          MISS
    sub s6 :lvalue { vec($s,0,8) }     perl writes through   PCL copies          MISS
    sub s7 :lvalue { $h{k} }           perl writes through   PCL copies          MISS
    sub s8 :lvalue { $a[0] }           perl writes through   PCL copies          MISS

So the ONE shape that works is the one that needs nothing, and every shape
that needs the feature loses the identity.  A half-fix that lit up `f() = V`
for all `:lvalue` subs while the body still returned a copy would convert 33
LOUD drops into 33 SILENT WRONGS -- the project's worst failure mode -- unless
the runtime setter dies on a non-box, which is the design note below.

WHAT THE FEATURE ACTUALLY IS: LVALUE CONTEXT propagated into the sub body's
tail and `return` positions.  Every piece already exists in the runtime; what
does not exist is a compile mode that selects them:
    element        p-aref-box / p-gethash-box   (the EAGER lvalue accessors;
                   the s455 boxed-aggregates model returns RAW elements from
                   the rvalue accessors, which is why s7/s8 miss)
    substr/pos/vec p-substr-lvalue-cell / p-pos-lvalue-cell / p-vec-lvalue-cell
                   (magic cells; `box-set` ALREADY delegates to their setters,
                   cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~line 2237)
    @_ element     the argbox path
    `return EXPR`  the return family copies; it would have to carry the box
So the work is: (1) record the `: lvalue` attribute -- `Pl::Environment` ALREADY
has `lvalue_subs` / `is_lvalue_sub` / `add_lvalue_sub`, and they are DEAD API,
called only by `Pl/t/environment-01.t`; nothing in the compiler populates them;
(2) compile the marked sub's tail + every `return` in LVALUE context; (3) drop
the compile-time die in `Pl/ExprToCL.pm:1474` for a known lvalue sub and emit a
set-through-return form; (4) a RUN-time `(p-die "Can't modify non-lvalue
subroutine call ...")` when the returned thing is not a box -- which is also
what a code-ref call needs, since `&$r(0) = 7` and `$a->() = 8` cannot be
classified at compile time (perl defers those to run time too).

THE TARGET FILE IS A TORTURE TEST, not a feature demo.  t/op/sub_lval.t's 33
lvalue drops need, beyond the eight shapes above: whole-array and whole-hash
returns in list context (`sub array :lvalue {@array}`, `sub hash :lvalue
{%hash}`), array and hash SLICES (`sub aslice1 :lvalue { @array[0,2] }`),
`keys` as an lvalue, tied pad variables, AUTOLOAD declared `:lvalue` in a
string eval, and deliberate temporaries/read-only returns whose ERROR text the
file asserts.  Current suite verdict: `op/sub_lval.t 211 planned, C_ok 54,
C_notok 47, DIFF, 34 drops` -- 101 of 211 rows produced.

COST ESTIMATE: 1 session for shapes s1-s8 plus the compile-side marking and
the run-time refusal (which would remove the 6 lvalue drops OUTSIDE sub_lval.t
-- substr.t x2 twice, signatures.t, try.t -- and an unmeasured part of
sub_lval.t's 33).  The list-context half (whole aggregates, slices, keys) is a
SECOND session and is what most of sub_lval.t actually exercises.  Do not start
this in a parallel round: it touches sub lowering and the return family, which
collide with the VarAnnotator/sub_info owner.

BAR when it is taken: the eight-shape table above matches perl on both emission
paths; `sub_lval.t`'s C_ok rises and every new C_notok is read and attributed;
the four non-sub_lval.t files' drops leave the census with cause; full sweep
(the runtime accessors are on every element path); guards inverse-verified.

s461ar resume note: NOT started, by the round's own instruction -- the 39
lvalue drops stay LOUD and the sizing above is the deliverable.  The census
totals moved for an unrelated reason (task #931 removed t/re/pat.t's row), so
this family is now 39 of 57 drops rather than 39 of 58.

=== USER DECISION (s464, 2026-09-02): DEFERRED â "worth doing, but we can push it a bit forward" ===
Asked how common `:lvalue` subs are on CPAN.  Measured locally (grep for a `: lvalue`
sub attribute): the installed perl 5.40.3 privlib + sitelib (755 + 234 .pm files) hold
TWO real definitions â core JSON::PP::incr_text (the incremental-parser accessor) and
core Thread::Queue::limit â plus support code in Class::Method::Modifiers (it PRESERVES
the attribute when wrapping) and documentation in attributes.pm / Sub::Util; ~/.cpan/build
(2432 .pm) adds no new ones; cpan-tests/ (94 .pm) has ZERO.  A MetaCPAN-wide count was
started (grep.metacpan.org API answers; the count was still running) and abandoned by
the USER: "so it exists, but isn't that common".  Decision: #964 (ordinary subs return a
COPY) ships FIRST and ALONE (agent s464a); this task keeps its sizing and its place in
the queue behind the round-21 correctness pool.  Its switch is the `p-sub-frame` macro
#964 introduces: an `:lvalue` sub is emitted with a frame that omits the copy.
subject: user `:lvalue` subs: SIZED with a measured 8-shape table -- 7 of 8 return shapes lose the box, so it is lvalue-CONTEXT propagation, not a bounded fix
